fixes.explanation: It's actually true. The second time he writes the line, Paul finishes it with “but I will not be mastered by anything.” He's saying nothing gets to boss him around. That's different from the first "but," which was about what's beneficial.

You've got it. Paul says the body is “…for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.” It goes both directions. The body isn't a spare part sitting in a drawer, and I would know, since I spent years in a junk drawer myself. It belongs in the Lord's hands, and I can tell you hands are a good place to be.

Look at the order Paul uses. God raised the Lord from the dead, and “…He will raise us also.” Raising someone from the dead is a different promise than keeping someone from dying. The verse names the raising.

Right, friend. Paul says, “…he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body?” Then he backs it up with Scripture: “The two will become one flesh.” He's showing that the joining is real, and he says so plainly.

Paul says the opposite. He writes that such a man “…is one with her in body?” Paul backs that up with the Scripture he quotes about two becoming one flesh. He describes the man as one with her, right in the middle of it.
Wealth doesn't come up in that verse. Paul says the one who unites himself with the Lord “…is one with Him in spirit.” The verse is about being joined to Him.

You've got it. Paul says, “Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.” That's why he gives the short command first: “Flee from sexual immorality.” Paul puts that command right at the front.

Paul doesn't talk about who can see it. His point is where the sin lands: “…he who sins sexually sins against his own body.” That's what he sets against every other sin, which he says is outside the body. He keeps the focus on the body.

That's the one, friend. Paul writes, “Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you…?” The Holy Spirit lives in them. That makes the body a special place, not just the thing that gets you to work on time.
A tool sits in a toolbox. Paul says something bigger: “…your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you…” That's a place for the Holy Spirit, not just equipment.
Yes, friend. Paul writes about “…the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God?” They received Him from God, and it's right there in the same verse as the temple.

Paul says the opposite right before his command. He writes, “You are not your own; you were bought at a price.” Then comes the "Therefore" and he tells them to “…glorify God with your body.” So keeping it for themselves isn't what he tells them.
